## What the completed parallelization controls establish

The now-implemented opt-in Ready policy removes the requirement to publish
finished work in original ID order. It uses the shared native pool and preserves
per-source accepted callback prefixes and completed holes for recovery. Admission
and its ownership transaction still have one coordinator: this is **not** a fully
sharded sector scheduler, and it does not sustain 50 busy cores.

Both worker matrices use the same frozen normal-release executable `8f725507…`,
all 67 saved owner programs and 8,179 nonidentity routing transports. The required
entry is restricted to one owner with R<=2, A<=11, D>=9: exactly 1,324 integer
starting tuples. All descendants are retained; no auxiliary initial cover or
prior checkpoint is used. This is a complete small recursive control, **not**
the full five-loop workload or a new IBP-generation timing.

| Workers | Ordered traversals (s) | Ready traversals (s) | Interpretation |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 6 | 363.557 / 362.790 | 382.723 / 388.450 | Ready is 5.27% / 7.07% slower |
| 50 | 312.792 / 317.517 | 238.349 / 234.753 | First clean pair: Ready 23.80% faster |

Every process reaches zero pending obligations/frontiers/failures with a drained
worker pool, queue and ledger. Independent phase-aware audits visit 5,094,173
W6 records and 5,108,457 W50 records, resolving every alias and initial anchor.
These audits are not a new symbolic proof of every saved IBP identity.

In the first clean W50 pair, Ready spends 11.06% more whole-command CPU and
performs 1.54% more native inspections for its 23.80% shorter traversal. The
reverse pair also favors Ready, but **Ordered2 overlaps the full live checkpoint11
write**. Preserve that measurement and confound; do not present two clean repeats.
Descriptive mixed-condition medians are 315.154 versus 236.551 s, with 9.24% more
CPU and 1.71% more native work for Ready. They are not statistical guarantees.

Sampled interior walking windows use roughly 6.96/6.93 busy cores for Ordered
and 10.33/10.21 for Ready. These exclude preparation, final save and output;
W6 traversal-only CPU cannot be recovered from its retained logs. Preparation
itself takes about 85–86 s because each process loads/verifies the full routing
manifest. Neither reserved workers nor active slots should be labelled CPU use.

Raw evidence: `TMP/ready-five-loop-finite-v2.83u7I3/` and
`TMP/ready-five-loop-finite-w50.a6ABXd/`. The latter contains complete results,
metrics, CPU-window analysis, checkpoint-overlap receipts and independent audit.
All eight native controls and their guards have exited; none is left running.

## Recovery: the important unresolved gate

Earlier Ready tests genuinely restored two saved multi-prefix states and passed
partial-progress checks. A negative missing-prefix checkpoint test also passes.
They do not establish full resumed exhaustion.

The new finite attempt in `TMP/ready-five-loop-full-resume.IQlQAN/` pauses
cleanly with exit4. However, by the actual checkpoint save, **zero positive
unfinished source prefixes remain**. A later successfully finished hole remains,
but that alone does not satisfy the planned gate. The result is inconclusive:
no resume, second attempt or automatic retry was launched.

A paused-report reader first encountered an absent optional `error` field; that
original harness failure is retained. Its narrow correction is pure-tested for
absent/null/non-null values and cannot change the inconclusive saved state.
An optional auditor scan also hit an old temporary numeric-parser limitation;
it is not counted as a successful scan or a native/checkpoint failure.

The trigger-to-first-cancellation heartbeat delay was about 1.007 s and
trigger-to-saved heartbeat 1.513 s. The CLI stop-file watcher may wait up to its
one-second polling cycle, during which almost 99,000 events advanced. These are
observed heartbeat intervals, not exact stop-file detection timestamps.

For a future authorized test, the existing coordinator `maybe_save(&State)` seam
could request cancellation synchronously when the real state has multiple
accepted prefixes and a finished hole, then save and fresh-process resume to
exhaustion. This is a source-only proposal, not implemented. There is no need to
weaken the gate or hunt for a bigger, slower mathematical input to trigger it.

## Other findings, including negative results

| Candidate | Measured or reviewed result | Current status |
|---|---|---|
| Application-cell refinement | Old slow head: 7.44→3.40 s, but 55.46% more successors. New head: 44.424→44.426 s. Four-parent recursive sum 1.74% slower. | Implemented opt-in; remains off |
| Admission minimum grain 8 | Four matched 24-helper pairs have exact equal state; median paired loop ratio 0.99885, preparation slower in every pair. | Test-only seam; production iterator unchanged |
| Adaptive initial-D overlap cut | Two opposite-order local comparisons reduce wall 10.36–15.06% and successors 15.49%. | Generic planner design only; recursive/recovery effects untested |
| Cross-inspection positive inclusion memo | 18.59M non-exact global reuse requests in the finite Ordered control, but repeated-full-key fraction unknown. | Observation instrumentation only; no cache implemented |
| Joint source-support mask pruning | Reviewed necessary degree inequality can reject jointly impossible pinches that separate column bounds admit. | Design only; effectiveness unknown |
| Independent entry shards | Exact 1,000/324-tuple split of the finite input could compare two W25 queues with one W50 queue. | Design only; duplicate descendant work and total cost unknown |

The proposed joint-support bound needs no new CAS kernel: for removed target
columns S, union the inactive source rows U(S) that can feed them using the
existing Symbolica-tested transport incidence. Available degree is bounded by
`min(sum of upper powers over U(S), R - mandatory lower powers outside U(S))`.
Reject only if the sum of denominator-cancellation costs exceeds this bound.
For example `(y1+y2+y3)*y4^9` has total degree10 and can cancel either y1 or y2,
but cannot cancel both simultaneously. Source rows must be counted once, not
once per target. This necessary bound received mathematical review; an admitted
family witness, exhaustive native endpoint tests and performance checks are
still required. No pruning code or performance claim is delivered here.

The finite control issues 28.4 million scheduling requests; 95.52% already reuse
existing obligations. Reuse happens after substantial matching/geometry work and
often after another containment search. Route inspections are 71.94% of native
jobs, not necessarily CPU; 73.85% of examined routing masks are already pruned.
Geometric routing overcovers can lose correlations. None of these counts proves
which additional jobs are avoidable or that a proposed optimization is faster.

The new spectator is entirely `cfg(test)`: bounded full-key FIFO observations,
source-identity attribution, comparison-cost counters, bounded destination maps,
and a cooperative stop watcher. It never serves a cache hit, changes admission,
claims coverage or adds a production API/schema. Generic arity and collision
tests, RAII cleanup and test-counter isolation received independent source review.
The native measurement is explicitly **deferred at the user's stop request**;
no repeated-key hit rate, memory benefit or speedup is claimed.

Final verification passes: the optimized application-library test build exits
successfully; all 8 focused spectator tests pass (the native measurement is
ignored). The same frozen binary then passes **641 default library tests**, with
0 failures and 4 ignored, in 63.37 s. The focused eight are included in that

checkpoint-prefix replay tests actually execute; they do not replace the open

The completed W50 timing controls above are separate evidence. Independent
source, receipt and handoff audits pass.
This optimized test build is not a production performance benchmark. Both build
and verification guards exit cleanly and are reaped; no diagnostic process is
